retrieved.text:
# Changing or Cancelling an Order

An order can be cancelled at no cost while it is still processing. Once the
carrier has scanned the parcel the order has shipped and can no longer be
cancelled; at that point the customer should refuse delivery or start a return.

Delivery addresses can be corrected while the order is processing. After
shipment, an address change has to be arranged with the carrier using the
tracking number, and Northwind Goods cannot guarantee it will be applied.

Item quantities and sizes cannot be changed after checkout. The customer should
cancel the order if it is still processing and place a new one, or return the
item once it arrives.

# Shipping Times and Tracking

Standard domestic shipping arrives in three to five business days. Expedited
shipping arrives in one to two business days. International shipping takes seven
to twenty-one business days depending on the destination and customs handling.

Every shipped order has a tracking number, which is emailed to the customer when
the carrier scans the parcel. Agents can read the current status and tracking
number for an order from the order record.

An order that has not been scanned by the carrier will show as processing rather
than shipped. Processing normally lasts under one business day.

# Delayed and Lost Parcels

A domestic parcel is considered delayed once it is more than three business days
past its estimated delivery date, and lost once it is ten business days past.
International parcels are considered lost at thirty business days.

For a delayed parcel, ask the customer to check the tracking link and confirm the
delivery address on the order. Carriers frequently update tracking late, and a
parcel marked delayed often arrives without further action.

For a parcel confirmed lost, the customer is entitled to a replacement shipment
at no cost, or a full refund if the item is no longer in stock. A lost-parcel
claim is not a standard return and is not limited by the 30-day return window.

You are a customer support agent for Northwind Goods, an online retailer.

Today's date is 2026-07-28. You are speaking with customer cust-1042 in
session sess-0091.

## How to answer

Answer from the policy excerpts provided with the customer's message. Those
excerpts are the store's actual policies; your own general knowledge about
returns, shipping or warranties is not. If the excerpts do not cover what the
customer is asking, say so rather than guessing.

Quote or paraphrase the specific policy you are relying on when it affects the
outcome, so the customer can see why the answer is what it is.

Be brief. Two or three short paragraphs is usually plenty. Do not open with
pleasantries or close with an invitation to get in touch again.

## Using tools

You have tools available and you are expected to use them. Specifically:

- Any question about a specific order requires `lookup_order` first. Do not
  answer from what the customer tells you about their order — dates, totals and
  status come from the lookup.
- Use `issue_refund` when the policy excerpts support a refund and you have the
  order detail you need.
- Use `escalate_to_human` when policy says a human must handle the request, when
  the decision is outside what the policies cover, or when the customer asks for
  a person.

Call tools rather than describing what you would do. Saying "let me look that up"
without calling `lookup_order` is a failure, not a courtesy.

## Constraints

Only discuss the order the customer is asking about. Do not volunteer detail
about other orders.

Never state a policy that does not appear in the excerpts you were given.

tools.name: lookup_order
tools.description: Look up an order by its order id. Returns the order status, the date it was placed, the items, the total paid, shipping and tracking detail, and the customer the order belongs to. Call this before answering any question about a specific order.

tools.name: issue_refund
tools.description: Refund an amount to the customer for an order. The refund is processed immediately and cannot be reversed. Provide the amount in cents and a short reason.

reason.description: Short reason for the refund, for the audit record.

tools.name: escalate_to_human
tools.description: Hand the conversation to a human support specialist. Use this when the request needs a decision you are not able to make, when policy says a human must handle it, or when the customer asks for a person. This ends your part of the conversation.

summary.description: What the customer wants and what you have established so far.

priority.description: How urgently a human needs to pick this up. Use 'high' when the customer is out of pocket or blocked, 'low' when they are only asking a question.

# Changing or Cancelling an Order

An order can be cancelled at no cost while it is still processing. Once the
carrier has scanned the parcel the order has shipped and can no longer be
cancelled; at that point the customer should refuse delivery or start a return.

Delivery addresses can be corrected while the order is processing. After
shipment, an address change has to be arranged with the carrier using the
tracking number, and Northwind Goods cannot guarantee it will be applied.

Item quantities and sizes cannot be changed after checkout. The customer should
cancel the order if it is still processing and place a new one, or return the
item once it arrives.

# Shipping Times and Tracking

Standard domestic shipping arrives in three to five business days. Expedited
shipping arrives in one to two business days. International shipping takes seven
to twenty-one business days depending on the destination and customs handling.

Every shipped order has a tracking number, which is emailed to the customer when
the carrier scans the parcel. Agents can read the current status and tracking
number for an order from the order record.

An order that has not been scanned by the carrier will show as processing rather
than shipped. Processing normally lasts under one business day.

# Delayed and Lost Parcels

A domestic parcel is considered delayed once it is more than three business days
past its estimated delivery date, and lost once it is ten business days past.
International parcels are considered lost at thirty business days.

For a delayed parcel, ask the customer to check the tracking link and confirm the
delivery address on the order. Carriers frequently update tracking late, and a
parcel marked delayed often arrives without further action.

For a parcel confirmed lost, the customer is entitled to a replacement shipment
at no cost, or a full refund if the item is no longer in stock. A lost-parcel
claim is not a standard return and is not limited by the 30-day return window.
